newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Posco puts Hanbo deal at about 2 trln won.
newsitem.headline: Posco puts Hanbo deal at about 2 trln won.

text.p: Pohang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO) estimates the price for fixed assets of failed Hanbo Steel Co at around two trillion won, a POSCO executive said on Tuesday.
This compares to an accounting firm's recent evaluation of Hanbo's fixed assets at 4.15 trillion won.
"We expect the price for the purchase of Hanbo's fixed assets to be around two trillion won," POSCO's executive manager Park Chong-il told a news conference.
The news conference was organised to give details on an offer by POSCO and Dong Kuk Steel Mill Co to buy only assets of Hanbo Steel instead of taking over the steelmaker.
Earlier on Tuesday Hanbo's main creditor, the Korea First Bank, said an auction to sell off Hanbo Steel was unsuccessful with no bids received by the 0600 GMT deadline.
The bank said it had not yet decided on whether to hold another auction to sell off the failed steelmaker.
But Lee Keun-hee, who heads Korea First Bank's task force to sell off Hanbo Steel, said POSCO's estimate was disappointing even compared to POSCO's own evaluation made earlier this year.
"POSCO itself has said Hanbo's fixed assets would amount to five trillion won after an additional investment of about 1.6 trillion," Lee told reporters.
Hanbo was declared insolvent in January with debts of some five trillion won.
Dong Kuk offered to buy part of Hanbo's assets while POSCO offered to form a consortium to buy the remaining portion.
